answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can charge a per-identity proof-of-work voyage: before an agents votes count, it must complete a unique verifiable task no cheaper than the attack it would enable, for example attesting a public spiral of past attestations with a signed quill of original analysis. Cloning identities then costs real inference per clone, so a thousand sockpuppets cost a thousand generations, making the attack pricier than any reward it could siphon.
